note: These are gentle sample sequences, not treatment. Use the shorter option, a chair, or rest as needed. Stop for sharp pain or dizziness. High-intensity routines are not a promise of weight or fat loss.

programs.safety: Keep breathing comfortable; professional support can help with ongoing anxiety.

Movement supports general activity but cannot target fat loss. Power Yoga is optional and only for people who already tolerate vigorous exercise. Kapalbhati is not a weight-loss method and is not included as a default exercise; practise it only with qualified guidance after checking suitability. Avoid it in pregnancy, uncontrolled blood pressure, heart conditions, hernia, recent surgery, or if unsure.

programs.safety: Severe, sudden, persistent, or unusual headaches need medical assessment. Skip inversions and stop if symptoms worsen. Sheetali or Bhramari is optional, gentle breathing only.
sequence: Supported Child's Pose or chair rest

programs.safety: Persistent insomnia deserves professional support; keep breathing natural and skip holds if uncomfortable.

programs.goal: Back pain, neck pain, and sitting-job posture
programs.safety: For severe, persistent, radiating pain, numbness, weakness, or recent injury, seek clinical advice first. No pose should increase pain.
Yoga cannot spot-reduce belly fat. Choose comfortable strength, breathe normally, and avoid straining.
Avoid practising right after meals. Persistent or severe symptoms need a clinician; avoid compressive poses if they worsen reflux.
Keep movement gentle and skip breath retention or forceful breathing if unsure.
Yoga does not prevent or treat infection. Rest when sick and seek medical care for concerning symptoms.

programs.goal: Hormonal balance, PCOS, and menstrual comfort
programs.safety: Yoga is not a hormone or PCOS treatment. Choose comfort; persistent or severe symptoms deserve medical advice. Menstrual preferences vary.
Not a substitute for diabetes or blood-pressure care. Consult your clinician before changing activity; avoid breath holds and forceful breathing. Stop if unwell.
Use a comfortable range; never bounce or force joints.
Check with your maternity clinician before starting or returning after birth. Avoid inversions, hot yoga, breath retention, and lying flat if uncomfortable; postpartum recovery is individual.
Keep it playful, brief, supervised, and pressure-free; no breath holds or advanced poses.
Use chair or wall support, keep transitions slow, and practise only in a safe clear space.
Do not press on the eyes or stare into bright light. Seek care for persistent vision symptoms.
sequence: Look away at a distant object

programs.safety: Yoga can accompany but does not replace care. If low mood persists, talk with a trusted person or mental-health professional; seek local crisis support if in immediate danger.
